subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should OpenClaw own Slack token rotation, and if so what credential store, refresh owner, and runtime adoption model should replace the current static Slack token contract?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose where one-use Slack refresh tokens and client secrets live, how refreshed tokens are committed, or how failures recover without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
options.body: Add a deliberate Slack plugin credential lifecycle with secure storage, atomic refresh replacement, reload/status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack validation.

options.title: Defer to external rotation
options.body: Keep static-token OpenClaw behavior and document an external rotation daemon/manual operational pattern until maintainers are ready to own rotating secrets.

options.title: Wait for generic rotating credentials
options.body: Defer Slack-specific work until OpenClaw has a shared plugin credential-refresh storage API that Slack can consume.

recommendation.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
recommendation.body: Add a deliberate Slack plugin credential lifecycle with secure storage, atomic refresh replacement, reload/status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack validation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest recent owner signal across the Slack runtime/config paths and is already involved in the related Slack token-reload discussion.
